Package frc.robot.superstructure

Class StateManager

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.superstructure.StateManager
public class StateManager extends Object
Bridge between the Hackbots Turret API and the Gearcats RobotStateMachine singleton.

Why This Class Exists

The Hackbots Turret.java (copied from the Hackbots 2026 codebase) was written to call methods on a StateManager object â€” specifically robotPose(), aimParams(), and the shootReady trigger. The Hackbots codebase has a full Superstructure class hierarchy that owns all of this state, but integrating that whole architecture would require rewriting large parts of the Gearcats codebase.

Instead, this thin adapter delegates every call to RobotStateMachine.getInstance(), which already manages pose, aiming, and readiness for the Gearcats robot. Turret gets the interface it expects; we keep our existing singleton structure unchanged.

Design Pattern

This is a classic Adapter (or "wrapper") pattern:
  • The Turret (client) expects a StateManager with specific methods.
  • The RobotStateMachine (adaptee) already has the data but under different method names and as a singleton rather than a passed-in reference.
  • This class is the adapter â€” it bridges the API mismatch.

Lifecycle

One instance is created in RobotContainer and passed to both AimPrep (via Turret.track(state)) and directly to Turret.track(state). The same instance is safe to reuse because all methods delegate to the thread-safe (single-threaded robot loop) RobotStateMachine.

  • Field Details

    • shootReady

      public final edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.button.Trigger shootReady
      A WPILib Trigger that is true when the robot is ready to fire â€” meaning the shooter is at speed, the hood is at the correct angle, and the turret is tracking the target within tolerance.

      This is a public field (not a method) so it can be bound directly to other Triggers and Command factories using Trigger.and(), Trigger.onTrue(), etc. without allocating a new lambda each call.

      Polled every robot loop by the WPILib CommandScheduler.

  • Method Details

    • robotPose

      public edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d robotPose()
      Returns the current best estimate of the robot's field-relative pose (position + heading).

      Internally this calls RobotStateMachine.getPose(), which fuses wheel odometry with PhotonVision camera estimates filtered by distance from the odometry estimate.

      Used by Turret.track() to convert the field-frame aim yaw into a robot-relative turret mechanism angle: mechanismAngle = aimYaw - robotHeading + kForwards.

    • aimParams

      public AimParams aimParams()
      Returns the current lead-compensated shot parameters (yaw, pitch, speed, TOF, status).

      Internally calls RobotStateMachine.getAimParams(), which runs the full pipeline:

      1. LeadCompensator shifts the hub position to account for robot velocity during ball flight.
      2. ToFAim looks up pitch, speed, and TOF for the resulting virtual target distance.

      Returns AimParams.impossible() when no AprilTag pose is available or when no feasible trajectory exists within the hood angle and speed constraints.
